title: feat(nm2oricyclt2z): cyclic lex-largest Orient freeze t+1 vs t+2 on two-axis opposite z-probes: reverse HOLD, face HOLD, composition HOLD
science: opposite z-probes, cyclic lex-largest orientation at two cuts. Reports the headline hold/hold frozen across t+1 and t+2 and calls the freeze 'the present letter'. The freeze is forced, not discovered. Composition is forced: O(q,tau) is constant for all tau>=t(q)+1 (any step e in O(q) requires e in M(q+e), which forces t(q+e)=t(q)+1), so t+2 can never differ from t+1 and composition=HOLD carries zero information.
